extracted.intended_audience: college/university faculty, curriculum committees, and administrators responsible for general education and quantitative reasoning programs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for designating undergraduate courses as satisfying a campus quantitative reasoning/general education requirement, plus program-level practices for fostering and assessing quantitative literacy across the curriculum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course designation criteria for the quantitative requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The LU faculty approved a set of criteria for courses designated as meeting the quantitative requirement: 1) at least 50% of the final grade be based on evaluated quantitative exercises, 2) students do a substantial amount of quantitative work distributed over the course of the 10-week term, and 3) teachers provide explicit instruction in quantitative methods and quantitative reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During implementation, faculty submitted course proposals explaining how courses would meet these criteria; an advisory board operationalized the criteria, provided feedback, and the Committee on Instruction approved courses accordingly. (Original numbered criteria preserved.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Define specific learning objectives and expected level of quantitative expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should define particular learning objectives and the level of quantitative expertise expected of graduates rather than relying on broad course labels alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debates arose about whether abstract mathematical concepts (e.g., calculus) develop quantitative reasoning versus whether applied measurement/statistics in other disciplines provide sufficient sophistication. The advisory board initiated faculty discussions to specify learning objectives and expected competency levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize breadth of application and repeated practice for quantitative literacy (QL)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative literacy should emphasize breadth of application across contexts and repeated practice, not simply increasing mathematical abstraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conceptual work on QL emphasizes transfer, breadth of application, and repeated practice. Foundational mathematical skills contribute to QL, but abilities to critically apply foundational skills and interpret quantitative reasoning in diverse real-world problems are necessary (Steen, 2001). Advanced mathematics promotes abstraction, while QL moves toward applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit instruction and practice in quantitative methods within courses
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated quantitative courses must provide explicit instruction in quantitative methods and quantitative reasoning and offer students repeated opportunities to practice these skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty are encouraged to demonstrate, explain, and provide practice in the application of quantitative reasoning; students should complete substantial quantitative work distributed over the term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage faculty across disciplines to make quantitative reasoning explicit (across-the-curriculum practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: All faculty should point out how quantitative concepts they teach relate to applications in other disciplines to promote transfer of learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The literature on transfer suggests transfer is likeliest when teachers explicitly connect concepts to other disciplines. LU held luncheons and workshops to begin conversations about QL goals and the types of quantitative reasoning taught in various disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment: include student perception measures about quantitative work and feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: At course completion, collect student reports on types of quantitative work, opportunities to develop quantitative reasoning, usefulness of feedback, and self-reports of changes in quantitative reasoning skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LU implemented a quantitative-intensive course evaluation form asking these items; initial data (335 students, 21 courses) used 10-point scales to compare lower- and upper-level courses and inform program improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment: measure actual quantitative skills and implement periodic thorough reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond perceptions, programs should assess actual quantitative skills with a more thorough instrument on a regular schedule (proposed every five years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructors of quantitative courses will be asked to incorporate the assessment instrument as part of course requirements; an extensive form will be part of the regular evaluation cycle for the quantitative GER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate assessment items into standard course evaluations for ongoing monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a subset of quantitative-program evaluation questions in every course evaluation to ensure student perceptions remain part of the general education assessment plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LU incorporated a few questions from the extensive form into every course evaluation after collecting baseline perception data, to keep student perceptions a regular part of assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit about the types of quantitative reasoning and methods that promote QL
rubrics_metrics.description: Operationalize criteria to specify which types of quantitative methods (e.g., statistics vs. abstract calculus) best promote quantitative literacy given program goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some faculty argued for more emphasis on application (statistics) while others supported foundational abstract skills; the program must decide which emphases align with its QL goals and curricular constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement and credit policy must safeguard QL outcomes (AP credit and placement issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies allowing advanced placement (AP) credit or placement out of the requirement should be scrutinized to ensure they reflect sufficient development of quantitative reasoning skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LU allows AP credit to satisfy the requirement and permits placing into advanced calculus; some faculty worry AP credit doesn't guarantee QL. Assessment plans include examining how different types of disciplinary training relate to QL skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop quantitative-intensive courses targeted to humanities and fine arts contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Create two or three additional quantitative-intensive courses aimed at students in the humanities or fine arts, using familiar disciplinary contexts to improve mastery and transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research shows students master problem solving better in familiar contexts. Developing such courses may require interdisciplinary co-teaching and face scheduling/cost challenges, but would strengthen the curriculum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for practical curricular and staffing constraints when designing QL curriculum
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance ideal QL curriculum design (e.g., widespread statistics offerings) with practical constraints such as faculty workload, departmental capacity, and costs of co-teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LU noted pressure on statistics staffing when many majors require it and when students flock to statistics to fulfill the requirement; creating quantitative courses across humanities/fine arts can be costly and requires institutional planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use applied learning experiences, labs, and real-world projects to reinforce QL
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate applied learning experiences—labs, one-credit lab components, and real-world projects with industry or government partners—so students collect, analyze, and interpret real data tied to course topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include a precalculus-linked lab in biology where students conduct weekly experiments and analyze data; partnerships (e.g., Cold Spring Harbor) can provide lab space, internships, and senior projects. Applied experiences help students appreciate and transfer quantitative methods to subsequent courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogy: require and give feedback on students’ explanation of reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage instructors to ask students to explain the reasoning behind their quantitative work at all course levels and to provide useful feedback on quantitative exercises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Student reports showed higher frequency of explaining reasoning in upper-level courses; feedback and explicit instruction rated highly. Programs should aim to increase explanation-of-reasoning opportunities especially in lower-level courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional commitment and incentives are essential for sustained interdisciplinary reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Large-scale interdisciplinary curricular reform requires strong institutional commitment—financial and academic—including administrative encouragement and recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LU (and Farmingdale examples) highlighted administrative support such as merit increases, counting project involvement in tenure/promotion, and mini-grants ($700–$1000) that provided visibility and encouraged faculty engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project leadership and grassroots faculty involvement model
rubrics_metrics.description: Project leaders should coordinate and act as cheerleaders rather than run the project top-down; good ideas should be able to come from all participants and be implemented from the grassroots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach increases buy-in and implementation likelihood. Frequent meetings (e.g., twice a semester) and an institutional culture of interdisciplinary contact help sustain enthusiasm and project activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect multiple pedagogical approaches and view curriculum renewal as ongoing
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs should respect competing alternative instructional approaches and treat curriculum renewal as an ongoing process rather than a one-time implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given rapid changes across disciplines and varying legitimate pedagogies, continuous rethinking and redevelopment of curricula is necessary to keep QL goals aligned with current needs.
